children.text: Nostalgic Influencers
by: Casey Boettcher and Mehal Agrawal.

The pre-Tik Tok era provided an environment for social media creators like Emma Chamberlain and Lilly Singh to thrive. The idea of influencers was relatively new at this time, and creators often looked to relatability to create a connection with their audience. Lilly Singh was the first South Asian influencer to take off on Youtube as she developed dramatic comedic skits based on everyday South Asian stereotypes. Emma Chamberlain was one of the first creators to dismantle the consistent format of youtube videos and vlogs. Rather than editing out imperfections in her videos, she emphasized them to create a sense of relatability with the viewers, often young girls the same age as her. As the environment of the world evolved, our influencer’s content evolved as well. However, they have made an active effort to stay true to the brand that they established promoting a sense of nostalgia and connection in their audience. Lilly Singh has started to tailor her content on Instagram to reflect important issues in the world today such as mental health and feminism. Nevertheless, the delivery of this content is through comedic skits and humor which is how she had built her original brand on Youtube. Chamberlain went from being the eccentric, messy teenager, to a well rounded interviewer and figure in elite fashion. She has focused her content efforts more on dealing with mental health and societal pressures, simultaneously evolving with the world around her. This has helped our influencers preserve the connection with their older followers while building a brand that is popular today.
Lilly Singh:
”This tiny tube has me in a CHOKEHOLD”

I chose to analyze Lilly Singh’s instagram account because I used to watch her Youtube videos when I was younger. She began releasing Youtube content based on comedy sketches that had South Asian references. Her Youtube channel took off in 2014 and by 2017 she was expanding past her Youtube content. Since Singh’s initial popularity, her brand and identity has changed significantly. Today, Singh has expanded into television, acting, writing, and producing while using Instagram as a way to showcase her professional accomplishments and produce more humorous relatable content. She released her first documentary in 2016, A Trip to Unicorn Island and her first book in 2017, How to Be a Bawse. She also hosted A Little Late with Lilly Singh on NBC from 2019- 2021. Her brand is surrounded  by comedy, personality, and women empowerment. Her humorous content allows her to maintain her brand from youtube and a connection with longtime followers while reaching a new audience through her brand evolution.
Emma Chamberlain:
"I WENT TO PARIS FASHION WEEK"
Emma Chamberlain grew up in California and started posting on YouTube in 2016 when she
was 16. She began posting vlogs about fashion, hauls, everyday tasks and life in high school.
She posted a couple vlogs in school and her school ordered her to stop filming in school and
she eventually made the decision to drop out of high school her senior year. She was depressed
and experienced lots of anxiety and her parents agreed she could pursue YouTube full time.
She began to blow up in 2017 and had 6 million followers by 2018. Her videos include vlogging
with friends/fellow YouTubers, shopping at thrift stores, cooking/baking and GRWMs. All of her
vlogs were full of self-deprecating jokes, were edited chaotically and replicated her unfiltered
mind. She would often cut to clips of her editing the video showing her thoughts and reflections
on things in the vlog. Moments that most YouTubers would edit out like breaks between
thoughts, goofy faces, and stumbles over words, Chamberlain emphasized them with funny
filters, zoom-ins and abrupt transitions. This form of editing took over YouTube as many creators
began replicating it. Her editing techniques and vlog topics reflected life at the time as a teenage
girl so many viewers connected with her as they were going through the same time.
